claims.author: jeanpablojp
claims.harm: targets with heavy per-input initialization incur higher cumulative execution time when sharded across processes
claims.quote: utxo_total_supply builds a ChainTestingSetup inside the target body, so a datadir per input, and three shards of 680 take around 240s each against 200s for all 2040 in one process.

status_by.quote: You're right. utxo_total_supply is the last to finish in all 20 master runs I checked, and it runs for the last 86 to 214s of them, so my sentence was wrong.

claims.author: jeanpablojp
claims.harm: temporary directory creation fails when parent directory is read-only even without sharding, and directories survive SIGTERM
claims.quote: with a read-only parent the run dies in mkdtemp, and --corpus-shards 1 doesn't avoid it. It also survives a SIGTERM, left next to the corpus.

status_by.quote: fixed this in the latest push by having a temp dir for each job

claims.author: jeanpablojp
claims.harm: exiting on failure removes shard directories while other shards run, causing remaining shards to fail on read_file assertions instead of the real error
claims.quote: with the sys.exit(1) in here, the dir disappears under the shards that are still running, so on the standalone builds they die on the read_file Assert instead of on the input that actually broke.

status_by.quote: I guess this is fixed by having per-job tmp dirs for the shards.

claims.author: jeanpablojp
claims.harm: fuzz coverage metrics become per-process rather than per-target, preventing comparison of aggregate coverage across commits
claims.quote: cov: becomes per process... you can't compare coverage across a change any more. Could the shards be folded back into one line per target?

status_by.quote: I don't think it is possible to recover the coverage from the shards. I can only see compiling with coverage instrumentation and then using that.

notes: Initial assessment tracking jeanpablojp's Concept ACK and several resolved non-blocking concerns regarding tempdir handling, crash masking, coverage metric reporting, and target setup overhead.

participants.note: Concept ACK, but raised issues with temp dir handling, crash reporting under failure, coverage loss, and setup overhead

support.author: jeanpablojp
support.reason: On Windows and MSan where runtime is dominated by single long targets, sharding cuts the tail latency and yields clear wins.
